consumer: The 'monster has noticed the avatar' flag is consumed as a yes/no the engine EVALUATES via its perception predicate (monster->sees(avatar)), asking 'can this monster actually perceive the avatar right now?'
scope: per-monster perception of the avatar across the visible region around the avatar (each nearby monster's line-of-sight/light/concealment check against the avatar), not merely raw positions inside the render window
decisive_source: src/creature.cpp::Creature::sees — its body computes whether one creature can perceive another right now from range, light, line of sight, vehicle-rotation occlusion, night-invisibility, hide-place and crouch coverage; it returns the authoritative perception boolean rather than re-deriving 'noticed' from positions
divergence: A monster sits inside the export window (so it renders via Excerpts 2/3) but an opaque wall breaks line of sight (or darkness/concealment defeats perception) between it and the avatar: deriving 'noticed' from in-window position (S) flags it as having noticed, while Creature::sees correctly returns false
